lines.cap: Your security clearance, part two: investigation.
In part one, Alex's application reached DCSA. Now comes the investigation, where DCSA checks the facts.
Step five. While the full investigation runs, DCSA may grant temporary eligibility. You may hear it called an "interim."
It's based on your form and early checks, and it can let you start cleared work sooner.
It has limits, and not getting temporary eligibility is not a denial. It just means you wait for the final decision.
Those limits: temporary Secret doesn't cover Restricted Data, COMSEC, or NATO information. Those need a final decision.
And temporary eligibility can't last more than a year unless DCSA approves.
Step six: the background investigation. DCSA checks records like criminal history and credit.
How deep it goes depends on your level: a moderate-tier investigation for Secret, and a high-tier one for Top Secret.
Checks can include national databases, your fingerprints, your credit, and your education and employment history.
Investigators may interview you, your references, and people who know you. Top Secret investigations dig deeper.
An interview is your chance to explain anything on your form. Keep a copy of your SF 86 handy, and if you don't know an answer, say so.
lines.say: An interview is your chance to explain anything on your form. Keep a copy of your S F eighty-six handy, and if you don't know an answer, say so.

lines.cap: If you speak to an investigator, answer promptly and honestly.
DCSA investigators carry an official DCSA credential card.
And if you're unsure an investigator is legitimate, DCSA can verify them. You can contact DCSA by calling 878-274-1186.
lines.say: And if you're unsure an investigator is legitimate, DCSA can verify them. You can contact DCSA by calling eight seven eight, two seven four, one one eight six.

lines.cap: Investigators don't decide your clearance. They gather the facts and report them to an adjudicator.
While you wait, you can follow your case status online in DCSA's Individual Engagement Platform.
lines.say: While you wait, you can follow your case status online in D C S A's Individual Engagement Platform.

lines.cap: And keep your FSO posted about changes, like a foreign trip or a new arrest. Reporting rules already apply while your case is in process.
lines.say: And keep your F S O posted about changes, like a foreign trip or a new arrest. Reporting rules already apply while your case is in process.

lines.cap: That's the investigation: temporary eligibility if you qualify, then record checks and interviews.
When it's done, the results go to an adjudicator. That's part three.
